newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Germany to tender crude oil in August.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Germany to tender crude oil in August.

text.p: Germany said on Monday it would start putting its strategic crude oil reserves out to tender in stages in early August and that each tranche would be 450,000 cubic metres, or about 2.8 million barrels.

The German government plans to raise around 400 million marks from the series of tenders that will start in the week beginning August 4 and continue until the end of the year, an Economics Ministry spokeswoman said.

Bonn plans to sell off over 50 million barrels of crude oil, about 20 percent of its total strategic reserves set up in the early 1970s. The spokeswoman said the sales would continue in 1998 raising a further 500 million marks.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet approved part of the sale on Friday when it passed a supplementary budget for 1997 and draft 1998 budget including plans for the tender this year and in 1998. Parliament must now vote on both budgets.

The move is intended to help Bonn lower its budget deficit to help it qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1997 -- the crunch year when economic data determine which countries can join the planned 1999 launch.

But the International Energy Agency (IEA), representing the world's major industrialised nations, has criticised the sale saying it would be of a "significant" proportion, reducing German stocks by about 25 days of forward cover to 95 days. The IEA estimates Germany has some 10 percent of world reserves.
While traders and analysts have said the sale would be yet another blow for an already bearish oil market.
"The oil will be sold in successive tranches each of 450,000 cubic metres from tank reserves," the economics ministry said in a statement.
"A typical average quality should be a mixture of 50 percent Iranian Heavy, 25 percent Arabian Light and 25 percent (Iraqi) Kirkuk crude oil," it said.

The statement said 45 percent of the mixture consisted of heavy grades and had an average API specific gravity of 30.5 degrees, while the rest consisted of light to medium crude oil and had an average API rating of 35.5.
The oil reserves are now being stored by the Nord-West Oelleitungsgesellschaft mbH in salt caverns in the town of Etzel near the German port of Wilhelmshaven on the north coast.

They were stockpiled between 1973 and 1981 using 16 different types of oil, mainly heavy grades, in response to the 1970s energy shock which hit when Middle East oil producers ratcheted up the oil price fourfold.
The oil will be sold in tanks -- and each lot will be tested by an independent body to analyse its precise grade and quality, the statement said.
The sale of the oil is being organised by the Hamburg-based oil supply agency EBV, it said.

An EBV official said earlier that workers had started pumping the oil from the salt caverns into holding tanks in Wilhelmshaven. Analysts would test the quality of the oil when those tanks were full in about a week to 10 days time.
The official said that in each of the 1997 tenders up to 10 tanks would be available for sale. Each tank held between 30,000 and 100,000 cubic metres of oil.
"It will be an open tender," said the official on condition of anonymity. "Anyone who wants to can bid. They may bid for one tank or two tanks or all the tanks," he said.
